name: LN
description: LN returns the natural logarithm of a number, using base e (approximately 2.71828182845904).
tldr: Returns the natural (base-e) logarithm of a number.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The positive real number for which you want the natural logarithm.

basicExample.explanation: e⁰ = 1, so the natural logarithm of 1 is 0.

advancedExamples.title: Cancel with EXP
advancedExamples.explanation: Taking the natural log of e³ returns 3.

advancedExamples.title: Natural log of e
advancedExamples.explanation: The natural log of e is 1.

howItWorks: LN computes logₑ(number), the power to which e must be raised to equal the input. It is the inverse of EXP: LN(EXP(x)) = x for all real x, and EXP(LN(x)) = x for x > 0.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: The argument must be strictly positive; zero or negative values return #NUM!.
For other bases use LOG(number, base) or divide by LN(base).

commonErrors.fix: Pass a positive number; the natural log of non-positive values is undefined.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: LN works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What base does LN use?
faq.answer: The natural base e (≈2.71828). LN(x) = logₑ(x).

faq.question: How do I compute a log in another base?
Why does LN(0) give an error?
faq.answer: The natural log of 0 is negative infinity, which is undefined, so Excel returns #NUM!.
